add.agent.p: A pull request holds your design, not font files. After the merge the repository builds the fonts from your source. The rules are short: your own design, an open license, and a name that no other typeface has.
add.agent.say: Add this font to the WhateverFont library under my GitHub name.
add.p: You need a font that you made with WhateverFont, a GitHub account and the GitHub CLI. Your GitHub name goes on the font.
add.two.p: The second command copies your design into library/, checks that it builds, and prints the commands that open the pull request.

chars.p: Every font that WhateverFont draws starts with GF Latin Core, the set that Google Fonts requires: Western, Central and Eastern European, Turkish, Baltic and Welsh letters, the common signs, and combining marks that attach to any letter. On top of that come the Vietnamese alphabet, Pinyin, letters for Azerbaijani, Hawaiian, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa, fractions, small figures above and below the line, more currency and math signs, arrows and shapes. Modern Greek and Cyrillic are in it too: Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Bulgarian, Serbian, Macedonian and Kazakh. Point at a character to see its name.

fonts.lede: An agent drew each of these with this engine, from a short brief. Pebble Sans is the exception: it restyles Inter in one command. All of them are free under the SIL Open Font License. The library has every font and every style, a search by mood, and room for yours.
foot.fine: WhateverFont was made by Brian Zhou and is open source under the MIT License. All generated fonts are open source under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. This project was built on top of fontTools, skia-pathops, HarfBuzz, and Pillow.
hero.lede: WhateverFont is a tool that lets you create entire fonts from a description. You can use AI to create completely new fonts, or use the engine to remix existing ones. The tool is made to be customizable and rapidly iteratable, and supports English, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Polski, Čeština, Türkçe, Tiếng Việt, Íslenska, Yorùbá, ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi, Azərbaycanca, Ελληνικά, Русский, Українська, العربية, हिन्दी, 日本語, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 한국어 and more.
how.code: font.py, the whole design of a family
how.p: The agent doesn’t draw outlines. It picks numbers like weight and contrast and writes a short recipe for each letter. WhateverFont does the rest.
how.s1.p: A recipe draws each letter as centerline strokes: a stem, a ring, an arch, a bowl.
how.s2.p: An elliptical pen gives the strokes their thickness. One number sets the contrast and another the stress angle. Stems can swell into flares.
how.s3.p: Each side of a letter is straight, round, diagonal or open, and gets a sidebearing to match. Kerning then fixes the pairs that remain.
how.s4.p: fontTools writes TTF and WOFF2 for each style, and one variable font with every axis.
how.s5.p: Proofs come from the built files, shaped with HarfBuzz. The agent looks, measures, and edits until the proofs are right.
lib.foot: The code is under the MIT License. Every font in the library is under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, and its copyright stays with the person who made it.

start.agent.p: Then say, in Claude Code or any coding agent: “Use whateverfont. Make me a font that …” The agent writes the brief down, draws three directions, fixes what it sees in its own proofs, and gives you a review board. Tell it what to change until the font is right.

start.hand.p: whateverfont docs lists the reference pages, and whateverfont examples the sources of every font on this page.
start.p: WhateverFont is a Python package and a skill for coding agents. It needs Python 3.10 or later.
